name: webwolf
notes: UNVERIFIED in this build environment: no network here to pull the image or confirm the port/health path at runtime — the operator must verify on first launch. Canonical image source: OWASP WebGoat project on Docker Hub (webgoat/goatandwolf), the combined container that bundles WebGoat (HTTP 8080) and WebWolf (HTTP 9090, context path /WebWolf) in one JVM. This descriptor points the scanner at WebWolf only (container port 9090); the same container also exposes WebGoat on 8080 — pair with the separate 'webgoat' descriptor for the actual lab surface. WebWolf is the out-of-band collaborator/companion (catches mail, incoming HTTP requests, and hosts attacker files) used by WebGoat's SSRF/XXE/blind-callback labs — it is intentionally an OOB helper, NOT a planted-bug corpus, so ground_truth.kind is 'none': the meaningful metric here is false-positive count + crawl/discovery + performance, and every confirmed finding must be scrutinised as a candidate false positive, not scored for recall. Auth/reachability caveats: (1) WebWolf uses Spring Security form login at /WebWolf/login and most functionality (mailbox, incoming-requests log, file hosting) sits behind registration/login, so an unauthenticated crawl is deliberately shallow — /WebWolf/login returns 200 while /WebWolf/home 302-redirects to login. (2) Some goatandwolf images bind the servers to 127.0.0.1 inside the container by default, which makes the mapped port unreachable from the host; the env WEBWOLF_HOST=0.0.0.0 (and WEBGOAT_HOST=0.0.0.0) are set to force 0.0.0.0 binding (Spring relaxed-binding of webwolf.host/webgoat.host). This is a harmless belt-and-suspenders default — v8.2.2 predates the 127.0.0.1-default change on newer tags, so verify against the exact tag; the variable names have also shifted across releases. No external DB is required (WebGoat/WebWolf use an embedded store). JVM cold start can take 30-90s, hence the 180s health timeout. enable_oob is false because WebWolf is itself the collaborator, not a target that needs an external OOB endpoint. max_audit_requests=0 means unbounded audit traffic (bounded only by max_pages/max_depth), which is intended so FP behaviour is actually exercised.
